module purpose: neorv32_cpu_control takes instructions from the fetch front end (frontend_i), holds the instruction word and program counters in exe_engine and sequences them through an execute state machine, issues ALU, load/store, register-file and CSR control on ctrl_o, keeps the machine, debug and trigger CSRs (privilege level, mstatus, mie, mtvec, mepc, mcause, mtval, mtinst, mscratch, counter controls, dcsr, dpc, tdata), buffers exceptions and interrupt requests, selects the trap cause, performs trap entry and return, and returns CSR read data on csr_rdata_o.

use-case flows.value: dispatch of a fetched instruction: when frontend_i.valid is set and no trap is pending, the instruction word, compressed flag and PC are taken into the execute engine
instruction decode and execute sequencing: next execute state, immediate, and ALU, load/store and register-file control issued on ctrl_o
control-flow target: branch condition from alu_cmp_i and next PC from alu_add_i, mtvec, mepc, dpc or the debug addresses
CSR write: CSR address and read-modify-write data formed from the instruction and rf_rs1_i, written into the machine, debug and trigger CSRs when csr.we is set
CSR read data selected by csr.addr when csr.re is set and returned on csr_rdata_o
exception and interrupt events: buffered exception flags, pending and enabled interrupt requests, the prioritized trap cause and the trap-entry signal on ctrl_o
trap entry and return: pending-trap state, jump to the trap vector with capture of mcause, mepc, mtval and mtinst and the privilege change, and return through mret or dret
privilege-based protection: the effective privilege, mstatus.TW and the counter-enable bits decide whether CSR accesses, mret and wfi are legal; MPRV and MPP decide the load/store privilege
debug mode: entry on halt request, ebreak, single step or hardware trigger, jump to the park or debug-exception address, dcsr and dpc capture, and exit on dret
hardware trigger: comparison of tdata2 with the next PC when the execute trigger is enabled, recorded in hwtrig_fired
sleep: entry after wfi when the front end is halted and no wake-up condition holds, and exit on wake-up
counter control: counter halt settings and counter increment events delivered on ctrl_o
while rstn_i is '0': PCs to BOOT_ADDR, execute state to EX_RESTART, privilege to machine mode, and the CSRs, trap buffers, debug mode and trigger state cleared

Availability: the core must leave sleep when a buffered interrupt, debug mode or single step occurs; a stuck sleep state or lost wake-up stops execution. Integrity also applies to the sleep state delivered to the consumer of ctrl_o.cpu_sleep, which is not supplied. sleep_mode stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 1028; CARRIES ctrl_o.cpu_sleep). trap_ctrl.wakeup computes (GATED_BY csr.dcsr_step, occurrence 4, line 1036). frontend_i sets the halted condition (field halted GATES sleep_mode, occurrence 8, line 1026). ctrl_o is the exit (field cpu_sleep COPIES sleep_mode, occurrence 38).
